High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioners are the persons whose land got under use and occupation of the Army by reference to the Jammu & Kashmir Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968.

entities.text: Jammu & Kashmir Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The use and occupation of the petitioners' lands is said to be dating back to the year 1960.
The petitioners used to receive rental compensation for the occupation of their land so held by the Army uptill the year 2013 whereafter the same got stopped getting paid to the petitioners.

The J&K Reorganization Act, 2019 has resulted in repeal of the Jammu & Kashmir Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968 and brings into operation the Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Act, 1952 which prescribes period of limitation for the requisitioned property to stay under requisition beyond which the requisition has to come to an end and reversion of the land has to take place.

entities.text: Jammu & Kashmir Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Act, 1952
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the time span has come to an end and yet the occupation of their land is continuing at the end of the Army for which they are in the present writ petition asking for quashment of the exercise made at the end of the respondent no. 7 under the repealed Jammu & Kashmir Requisition and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1968 in the Pritam Chand And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 7 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62768201/
1 form of a draft assessment report DCJ/LHS/Army/RAIP/JMU/CS325/96 dated 21.10.2014 and also asking for compensation from 2013 till 31.10.2020 and subsequent relief for damages for continuing occupation of their land by the respondents till the acquisition takes place under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 or the vacant possession of the land is handed over to the writ petitioners.
Prima facie case is made out.
Issue notice to the respondents.
Mr. Vishal Sharma, learned DSGI accepts notice on behalf of the respondent nos. 1 to 5 and Mrs.
Monika Kohli, learned counsel on behalf of the respondent nos. 6 & 7 and seek time to file response within a period of four weeks.
List on 31.07.2023.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE Jammu 07.06.2023
